rules.description: List of authorization rules; each rule defines who may run what as whom with which options. One rule per line in the config file. Order matters: first matching rule wins. The action must be 'permit' or 'deny'. The ident (optional) specifies the user(s) to whom the rule applies ('any' or a specific username). The targets (optional) specify the target user(s) (e.g. 'root'). The commands (optional) are the allowed commands (can include wildcards and full paths). Options may be an unordered list of valid doas.conf options per rule (e.g. 'nopass', 'keepenv'). 'log' is a boolean option that may appear alone as 'log'. No nested objects: all options are flat keys with boolean or string values as appropriate. See doas.conf(5) for full semantics. Every rule must contain at least 'action' and 'commands'. We allow 'targets' and 'options' to be omitted if empty/none. To avoid ambiguity, every rule must have at least: action, ident, commands. We represent options as a list-like dict of flag names to booleans. We'll define rule items with these keys: 'action' (string), 'ident' (string), 'targets' (list of strings), 'commands' (list of strings), 'options' (list of strings). This is the cleanest match: e.g. options: ['nopass', 'log', 'persist', 'cmd']. This matches the file format.
